messages:
Dan: Hey team — customer on Dedicated report intermittent 401s when calling Redwood API through their internal LB + Istio gateway. Works with same key when hitting hosted API. curl shows Authorization header present from client.

Alice S: thanks Dan. Can you paste the curl or the request-id from our logs? Also is this Dedicated in VPC (AWS) or on-prem?

Dan: It's AWS VPC, ALB in front -> nginx-ingress -> istio gateway -> service. curl: 
```
curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-test-xxxx' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 'https://api.dedicated.example.com/v1/complete'
```
Response: 401 {'error':'invalid_api_key'}

Ben P: classic header-dropping. ALB shouldn't drop Authorization but some middle proxies or ingress controllers may. First repro step: check what headers reach the app pod. Run from the istio-proxy sidecar or from the ingress pod: 
```
kubectl -n ns exec -it pod/redis-service -- curl -sS -D - -o /dev/null 'http://localhost:8080/health' -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-test-xxxx'
```
Or add a debug endpoint that dumps headers.

Carla I: also check nginx ingress config: nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-set-headers and proxy_hide_header/proxy_pass_request_headers. Many ingress charts default to hide 'Authorization'. For NGINX use: 
```
proxy_set_header Authorization $http_authorization;
```

Dan: I pulled logs from our app. I see no Authorization header in the request headers. Upstream client sends it though. So it's stripped somewhere between ALB and app.

Ben P: In Istio, the sidecar or virtual service is unlikely to drop header unless an Envoy filter is configured to remove it. But K8s Services with 'externalTrafficPolicy' or health checks can mutate. Also confirm AWS ALB listener rules — if ALB is doing AWS Cognito auth-action it will exchange tokens and inject Authorization differently.

Alice S: For a quick workaround you can configure the client to send api_key in a custom header e.g., 'X-Api-Key' and add an Istio EnvoyFilter to copy that into Authorization on the sidecar. Example EnvoyFilter snippet:
```
apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1alpha3
kind: EnvoyFilter
metadata:
  name: copy-x-api-key-to-auth
  namespace: default
spec:
  workloadSelector:
    labels:
      app: redwood-proxy
  configPatches:
  - applyTo: HTTP_FILTER
    match:
      context: SIDECAR_INBOUND
    patch:
      operation: INSERT_BEFORE
      value:
        name: envoy.filters.http.lua
        typed_config:
          '@type': type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.lua.v3.Lua
          inlineCode: |
            function envoy_on_request(request_handle)
              local h = request_handle:headers()
              if h:get('authorization') == nil then
                local k = h:get('x-api-key')
                if k ~= nil then
                  h:replace('authorization', 'Bearer ' .. k)
                end
              end
            end
```

Carla I: long term prefer fixing the ingress config so original Authorization is preserved. If using nginx-ingress-controller add annotation: nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-set-headers: 'ingress-nginx/custom-headers' and create configmap with proxy_set_header Authorization $http_authorization;

Dan: We tried adding proxy_set_header but still missing when request reaches service. I think ALB pre-auth with Cognito was enabled (we inherited infra). ALB auth will remove Authorization and replace with 'x-amzn-oidc-data' etc.

Ben P: If ALB auth is enabled you need ALB to forward the token via a header or skip ALB auth for API routes. Alternatively set up ALB to preserve original headers and pass along. Another option: terminate ALB auth and re-issue header as X-Forwarded-Authorization.

Alice S: Actionable steps we agreed:
1) Dan to confirm ALB listener rule and whether ALB auth action is on.
2) Carla to check nginx configmap and ingress annotations for proxy_set_header.
3) Ben to prepare EnvoyFilter Lua snippet as emergency patch to copy X-Forwarded-Authorization or X-Api-Key into Authorization.
4) Support to correlate request-id logs once header forwarding is fixed.

Dan: adding request-ids I saw for failing requests: req_2025_001, req_2025_002.

infra-bot: deploy started carla/ingress-config-update #456

Carla I: pushed configmap update with proxy_set_header, rolling restart ingress pods.

Ben P: I also opened a short-lived canary EnvoyFilter in namespace default. Monitor for 401s.

Alice S: Thanks everyone — I'll follow up with the customer with repro steps and ETA. :thumbsup:

Dan: Confirmed after envoy patch 200: we now see Authorization header at app and requests succeed. We'll schedule ALB auth config change next week.

Alice S: closing the escalation — keep thread open until ALB change.
